advances: A conditional statement about the exposed face of a chosen corrected resultant at a fixed buffered maximizer.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
At any sampled maximizing mark $(r,Y)$ the adjusted threshold in each selected direction is at most its right upper $Q$-quantile, since that tested cap has mass at least $Q$. Comparing with the right quantiles at $(p,y)$ gives
$$
d_j=a_j\cdot(r-p)+u_j\cdot(Y-y)-\varepsilon(f(r,Y)-f(p,y))\le0.
$$
By the two balance identities the weighted sum is
$$
\sum_j\rho_jd_j=\ell\cdot(r-p)+\varepsilon[f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(r-p)+g\cdot(Y-y)-f(r,Y)].
$$
The bracket is nonnegative. Thus $\ell\cdot(r-p)\le0$. If it equals zero, each $d_j$ is zero since the weights are positive. In particular the same physical regular cap and threshold binds at both marks.

Write $m(a,u,c)$ for the actual mass of the cap $a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge c$. At the regular row its derivative with respect to $c$ is strictly negative. To see this from positive total section coarea, choose a fiber whose section has positive $(d-1)$-measure. By taking convex combinations of that section with a fixed interior point off the section plane, parallel sections on one side of the cutting level have uniformly positive area sufficiently close to the level. This follows from containment of homothetic copies of the original section with ratios tending to one. Fubini in this fiber gives at least a constant times $h$ mass in the slab between levels $c-h$ and $c+h$ for small $h>0$. The other fibers add nonnegative slab mass. Hence the symmetric difference quotient of the full tail is strictly bounded above by a negative constant. Differentiability gives $\partial_c m<0$.

The implicit function theorem now makes the mass-$Q$ threshold $c_Q(a,u)$ differentiable near the regular row; its strict local decrease in $c$ and the global monotonicity of the tail identify the local threshold with the right upper quantile. Hold the normalized $u$ fixed. Feasibility at each of the two marks gives the inequalities
$$
a\cdot s+u\cdot X-\varepsilon f(s,X)\le c_Q(a,u)
$$
for all base tilts $a$, for $(s,X)=(p,y)$ and $(r,Y)$, with equality at the same fixed $a$. Differentiating each contact gives $\nabla_a c_Q=p$ and $\nabla_a c_Q=r$, using coordinates in the affine base span if it is lower dimensional. Thus equality of the resultant margin is impossible for $r\ne p$. The vertices of the exposed face belong to $I$, which proves that face is $\{p\}$.

For the polytopal assertion, assume the own trace is proper and no other supporting section has positive $(d-1)$-measure. Each full-area supporting section of a polytope must lie in one of its finitely many facets, with the cutting plane equal to its facet plane in continuous coordinates. Thus sufficiently near the given full parameters no such supporting section occurs in any fiber, and the own section stays proper. The section first-variation formula of 1269c554ca9a41b8 applies there, with zero contribution at each nonproper trace. On a proper limiting section its area and first moments vary continuously: identify nearby section planes by isometries tending to the identity, use compactness for outer convergence and approximate its relative interior by interior points of the body on the nearby planes for inner convergence. At a null supporting section, compactness confines the nearby sections to arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the zero-area limit after the same identifications, so their areas and moments tend to zero. Empty strict traces stay empty. In $d=1$ the nonempty supporting sections already have positive counting measure and are excluded by hypothesis. Therefore the first-variation coefficients are continuous. The locally uniform slab bound on changes of the cap mass makes the linear directional derivative a full derivative, by compactness of unit perturbation directions. This gives the claimed full $C^1$ regularity.

statement:
Fix a finite positive compatible mixed family and a fixed buffered depth with continuous covectors normalized in a fixed norm independent of the base tilt $a$. Let $(p,y)$ be a global sampled buffered maximizer, with value $Q$ and maximizing base set $I$. Suppose a chosen group of actual mass-$Q$ caps is
$$
H_j=\{(z,x):a_j\cdot(z-p)+u_j\cdot(x-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\},
$$
with thresholds equal to the right upper $Q$-quantiles of their fixed normals. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and suppose $\rho_j>0$, $\sum_j\rho_j=1$, $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$, with a full supporting bound
$$
f(z,x)\le f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(z-p)+g\cdot(x-y).
$$
The corrected resultant is $\ell=\sum_j\rho_j a_j-\varepsilon\alpha$. If at least one selected cap has $C^1$ actual mass as a function of its full hyperplane parameters $(a,u,c)$ near that cap and its total section coarea is positive, then
$$
\ell\cdot(r-p)<0\qquad(r\in I,\ r\ne p).
$$
Thus the face exposed by this particular resultant on $\operatorname{conv}I$ is $\{p\}$. If the fibers are polytopes and a selected row has a proper own section, failure of its full $C^1$ regularity requires a supporting section of positive $(d-1)$-measure in another fiber.
title: A regular buffered cap forces strictness of its corrected support
